mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about inflorescence is NOT correct?

options.A: Inflorescence is the arrangement of flowers on the floral axis of a plant.
options.B: Inflorescence refers to a single flower only.
options.C: Inflorescence includes the peduncle, rachis and pedicels that bear the flowers.
options.D: Inflorescences can be classified mainly as racemose or cymose.

mcqs.answer: Inflorescence refers to a single flower only.
mcqs.explanation: Inflorescence denotes the pattern in which multiple flowers are arranged on the floral axis; it is not limited to a single flower. Option B is the only statement that misrepresents the concept. Options A, C and D correctly describe inflorescence.

mcqs.question: In a typical racemose inflorescence, where are the youngest flowers located?

options.A: At the tip of the main axis
options.B: At the base of the main axis
options.C: In the middle of the axis

mcqs.answer: At the tip of the main axis
mcqs.explanation: Racemose (indeterminate) inflorescences grow continuously from the apex; therefore the apex bears the youngest buds while older flowers are positioned lower down. Hence the youngest flowers are at the tip (option A). The other positions describe determinate or non‑racemose patterns.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly differentiates a cymose inflorescence from a racemose inflorescence?

options.A: In cymose inflorescences the main axis continues to grow, while in racemose it terminates with a flower.
options.B: Cymose inflorescences are indeterminate, whereas racemose inflorescences are determinate.
options.C: The youngest flower in a cymose inflorescence is situated at the apex, while in racemose it is at the base.
options.D: Cymose inflorescences have a determinate growth pattern where the terminal flower blooms first, unlike the indeterminate growth of racemose types.

mcqs.answer: Cymose inflorescences have a determinate growth pattern where the terminal flower blooms first, unlike the indeterminate growth of racemose types.
mcqs.explanation: Cymose (determinate) inflorescences stop elongating because the terminal bud becomes a flower; subsequent flowers arise from lateral buds below it. Racemose (indeterminate) inflorescences keep growing, producing younger flowers at the tip. Option D accurately captures this contrast. Options A, B and C invert the characteristics.

mcqs.question: Which of the following plants exhibits a cymose (determinate) inflorescence?
mcqs.explanation: Tomato plants bear a determinate or cymose inflorescence where the main axis ends in a flower, and further growth occurs from lateral buds. Wheat has a spike (a type of racemose), lily shows a raceme, and sunflower possesses a capitulum, none of which are cymose. Hence option C is correct.
